logicalBugs.description: Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. Workspace picture uploads can save successfully while General settings shows the wrong result. A valid first upload can disappear from the preview and disable Remove after the first settled reload; repeated logo replacements can save the latest image but report an error and keep the previous preview. These cases concern supported image uploads, not rejection of non-image files.
logicalBugs.rootCause: uploadWorkspacePicture updates logoFileId directly in workspaceRepository without invalidating the cached workspaceEntity. The client initially displays the returned upload URL, but refresh can hydrate the older cached workspace without the new logo; replacement can also try deleting an already deleted logo ID.
reproductionPaths: Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. A valid workspace picture appears immediately after upload, but the first settled refresh of General settings can show an empty picture and disable Remove.

Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. Replacing an existing logo repeatedly on the same General settings page can save the latest image but return an error and retain the previous preview.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty settings have separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. After an unsupported upload breaks an image preview, a subsequent valid Profile or Workspace picture saves successfully but its preview remains blank or gray until reloading or reopening the editor.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ImageInput sets isPictureURLError on an image-load error and never clears it when pictureURI changes. A later successful upload remains behind the error placeholder in the same mounted component.
reproductionPaths: Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. After an unsupported upload breaks the profile picture preview, a subsequent valid image saves successfully but the preview stays gray until reloading or reopening the editor.

Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. After an invalid workspace-image upload, a later supported image saves but its preview stays blank in the mounted upload control.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. The Data model diagram can position record-type cards so their contents are not fully visible. Neighboring cards can overlap and cover fields or expansion controls; fitting the diagram can also clip the bottom of a card even though zooming out reveals it. These are diagram-layout failures, not deletion of the fields.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The diagram layout gives every object node a fixed 220x100 geometry in Dagre and React Flow even though the rendered card height grows with its field rows. Layout separation and Fit view use the short fixed rectangle, causing overlaps and clipped lower rows.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. The initial data-model visualization overlaps neighboring object cards, obscuring field and relationship rows and their expand controls.

Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Fitting the data-model diagram can leave the lower part of an object card outside the canvas, even though zooming out reveals the complete card.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Field previews in Data model settings can ignore the configured number of decimal places. Accepted examples include Currency previews dropping fractional digits, Percentage previews ignoring their precision and Number previews omitting required trailing zeroes. Reopening retains the settings, so this is preview formatting rather than loss of the configured precision.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CurrencyDisplay treats configured decimals as maximumFractionDigits through formatNumber, whose minimumFractionDigits is zero. Preview values ending in zeros omit the requested decimal places, including the TWD example.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Set a Currency field preview to Full format with two decimal places. The saved setting remains selected after reopening, but the affected currency preview omits its fractional digits.

Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Set a Percentage field’s preview precision to one decimal place. The preview ignores the configured decimal count.

Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Configure a plain Number field with a fixed decimal count. Its preview omits trailing zeroes rather than padding to that precision, despite the explicit fixed-decimal example.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Expanding AI Skill Instructions or Workspace Instructions at phone width can cover the settings form while hiding the controls needed to save or return. The enlarged editor provides no visible close or back route in the accepted cases. This concerns the mobile expanded editor rather than ordinary inline editing.
logicalBugs.rootCause: FormAdvancedTextFieldInput disables its fullscreen close control on mobile, while the mobile Settings breadcrumb may render no return control. Expanding Skill Instructions therefore removes the normal form Save context without exposing a reachable exit from the fullscreen editor.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Expand AI Skill Instructions at phone width. The enlarged editor hides Save and provides no visible way back to the Skill form.

Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Expand Workspace Instructions in AI settings at phone width. The editor covers the settings page while its close button and return breadcrumb (page navigation link) are hidden.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Long custom record type API names that pass local length validation can fail creation or rename because generated record link names exceed their own shorter limit. The form accepts the original object name without explaining the derived-name failure.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Object-name validation permits the object API-name length in isolation, but generated morph relation field names append object-specific suffixes and are checked against the same field-name maximum. A valid long object name therefore produces an overlength generated relation name during create/rename.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Create a custom record type with a singular API name that passes the form’s length limit. Creation can still fail because an automatically generated linked-field name is too long.

With label and API-name synchronization enabled, renaming an existing custom record type to a permitted long singular label generates an overlong related-field name and fails. The attempted rename remains a draft; a generic related-field validation error appears and reload restores the previous saved name.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty settings tables support sorting rows by clicking column headers. Sorting a settings table by a true/false property can replace the page content with an error screen. Accepted triggers are Type in the AI Skills list and Unique in the Companies Indexes table. The failure happens when sorting the table, rather than creating or saving the listed items.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Skills Type column declares the Boolean isCustom field as string. The shared sorter calls localeCompare on its Boolean value without conversion, throwing during list rendering.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Sorting the AI Skills list by Type throws a Boolean localeCompare error and replaces the settings page content with an error screen.

Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Open the Companies Indexes table in Data model settings and sort by Unique. The settings content is replaced by an error screen rather than sorting the rows.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Autosaving edits to AI Skill Instructions or Workspace Instructions interrupts the active text editor. The expanded editor can close, formatting menus can disappear or the input can lose focus during continued typing. This happens as the edit saves, rather than because the user intentionally leaves the editor.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Skill and Workspace Instructions hosts use their last saved rich-text content as the editor React key. Successful autosave updates that key and remounts the shared editor, dropping focus and resetting fullscreen/menu state.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Autosaving changed Instructions in a saved Skill reopens its editor, closing fullscreen and formatting menus and losing focus.

Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Successful Workspace Instructions autosave interrupts continued editing by closing the expanded editor or dropping compact-editor focus.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. Immediately regenerating an API key with a finite expiration repeatedly shortens its saved lifetime by roughly one additional day each time.
logicalBugs.rootCause: computeNewExpirationDate truncates the original lifetime to whole days with differenceInDays and adds that integer duration to the regeneration time. The sub-day portion of the original expiration interval is lost on regeneration.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. Immediately regenerating an API key with a finite expiration repeatedly shortens its saved lifetime by roughly one additional day each time.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Clearing an existing AI skill description appears to work, but reopening or refreshing the skill restores the previous description.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsSkillForm sends description: formValues.description || undefined for both update/save paths. Clearing a saved description becomes an omitted field rather than an explicit empty string, so the mutation leaves the previous description unchanged.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Clearing an existing AI skill description appears to work, but reopening or refreshing the skill restores the previous description.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. The workspace menu offers Invite user to members without invitation permission, but selecting it silently redirects to Profile instead of explaining that the action is unavailable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Invite user navigation action is exposed independently of the WORKSPACE_MEMBERS setting permission required by the Members/Invite route. The settings route guard redirects unauthorized members to their permitted Profile page without an explanation at the source action.
reproductionPaths: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. The workspace menu offers Invite user to members without invitation permission, but selecting it silently redirects to Profile instead of explaining that the action is unavailable.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. At a narrow browser width, ordinary mouse clicks on saved navigation folder contents fail to open their destinations until layout customization has been entered in the current session.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Navigation folder contents are wrapped in sortable/draggable items while navigation is delegated through NavigationDrawerItem click/mousedown handlers and mobile collapse state. In a fresh narrow session the drag/navigation boundary can consume pointer clicks before item navigation; exact first-session event ordering is not established by static inspection. Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. At a narrow browser width, ordinary mouse clicks on saved navigation folder contents fail to open their destinations until layout customization has been entered in the current session.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After a displayed custom field is deactivated and reactivated, it is active in Data model settings but remains absent from saved record Fields layouts.
logicalBugs.rootCause: activateMetadataField only updates isActive:true on field metadata. Deactivation has already removed/hidden the field from saved layout/view-field configuration, and activation does not recreate that placement, so the field becomes active without returning to its former record layout position.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After a displayed custom field is deactivated and reactivated, it is active in Data model settings but remains absent from saved record Fields layouts.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Dropdown option labels that generate the same API value disable Save without showing the collision error, even when the visible labels differ.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Select option API values are normalized from labels and the form schema rejects colliding normalized values. Save derives its disabled state from form validity, but the option row/API-value editor does not render the corresponding duplicate-value validation message beside the input.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Dropdown option labels that generate the same API value disable Save without showing the collision error, even when the visible labels differ.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. A user granted Roles permission without Users permission can edit roles directly, but the Roles breadcrumb (page navigation link) redirects to Profile and role-list navigation is absent.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The standalone Roles route is protected by ROLES but redirects to the Members page #roles, whose enclosing route requires WORKSPACE_MEMBERS. Navigation only exposes Members under that latter permission, so a roles-only user can reach role details but not the Roles list.
reproductionPaths: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. A user granted Roles permission without Users permission can edit roles directly, but the Roles breadcrumb (page navigation link) redirects to Profile and role-list navigation is absent.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Saved comma-decimal number preferences are ignored by abbreviated currency amounts and summary calculations in Opportunities (sales deals).
logicalBugs.rootCause: CurrencyDisplay uses formatToShortNumber for the default short representation instead of the locale-aware useNumberFormat formatter. Abbreviated opportunity amounts therefore retain the short helper decimal separator regardless of the selected comma-decimal preference.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Saved comma-decimal number preferences are ignored by abbreviated currency amounts and summary calculations in Opportunities (sales deals).

logicalBugs.rootCause: The diagram object title builds its link with SettingsPath.Objects, the generic catalog route, while supplying an objectNamePlural parameter unused by that route. It should target the per-object detail route.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. An API key configured to Never expires is displayed with a far-future calendar expiry in its role Assignment table.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Role assignment displays every truthy API-key expiresAt with formatDateString. The API-key Never expires representation is a far-future timestamp, so this surface formats the sentinel as a real date rather than using the API-key expiration formatter.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. An API key configured to Never expires is displayed with a far-future calendar expiry in its role Assignment table.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. The layout editor accepts a URL containing spaces and no valid hostname, publishing an unusable workspace navigation link.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Navigation link editing trims and applies ensureAbsoluteUrl but does not validate the resulting URL against a hostname/URL schema. Malformed text can therefore be saved as a link and opened by the regular external-link control.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. The layout editor accepts a URL containing spaces and no valid hostname, publishing an unusable workspace navigation link.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After editing a record type’s API name, existing indexes lose their field labels and cannot be found by field-name search. New index creation can intermittently cause the same display and search failure.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Index labels are reconstructed by matching indexField.fieldMetadataId to the current object fields. Object API-name mutation metadata can leave stale index-field IDs in the client object/index projection, so the unmatched entries are filtered out and the labels and label-based search become empty until consistent metadata is loaded. Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After editing a record type’s API name, existing indexes lose their field labels and cannot be found by field-name search. logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. At phone and tablet widths, closing a navigation customization panel leaves subsequent folder and link editors without their editing controls.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Side-panel close clears selectedNavigationMenuItemIdInEditModeState, while the narrow-layout close/reopen transition also reuses that same selection for editing. A late close/reset can clear the newly selected folder/link, and SidePanelNavigationMenuItemEditPage renders its empty selection placeholder. Exact effect ordering is inferred from the reported narrow-only transition. Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. At phone and tablet widths, closing a navigation customization panel leaves subsequent folder and link editors without their editing controls.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. A field that can link to several record types is saved as Belongs to one, meaning each source record selects one destination. Reopening its editor instead shows Has many and a matching incorrect preview, while the Relations list still reports the correct saved relationship type.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsDataModelFieldRelationForm initializes relationType only from existingFieldMetadataItem.relation?.type, then defaults to ONE_TO_MANY. Multi-destination fields store their relation legs in morphRelations instead, so their saved MANY_TO_ONE choice is ignored on reopen.
reproductionPaths: Twenty supports relationship fields with several possible destination record types. Save one as Belongs to one, meaning one selected destination per source record, then reopen it. The editor and preview say Has many instead, while the Relations list keeps the correct saved type.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Reset to default restores all Address subfields in the preview but the reset is omitted from saving, so reopening or refreshing retains the previously saved custom selection.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Address Reset to default uses resetField with a new defaultValue for settings.subFields. That changes the field baseline instead of marking an explicit user edit dirty, so canSave can remain false and the reset is not persisted.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Reset to default restores all Address subfields in the preview but the reset is omitted from saving, so reopening or refreshing retains the previously saved custom selection.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Saving a field that links to several destination record types can add several identical rows for the whole relationship to the settings list. Reloading collapses them back to one. The accepted failure is duplicate presentation of one configured relationship, not creation of multiple separate relationship fields.
logicalBugs.rootCause: A morph relation is represented by multiple per-destination field metadata records. Mutation draft application appends those rows directly to the metadata store, while full metadata hydration collapses them into one logical field. The Relations table therefore renders one duplicate per destination until refetch normalizes the representation.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Saving one multi-destination record link displays multiple identical whole-relationship rows until the page is refreshed.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After a duplicate field label or API-name rename is rejected, the editor can switch to the conflicting field while retaining the original field URL. Subsequent corrected Save or Delete then affects that other field.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsObjectFieldEdit sets newNameDuringSave before awaiting the rename and resolves the current field by either the original name or that pending name. A rejected duplicate rename leaves the pending name set, so find can select the other existing field and subsequent edits/delete act on its ID.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After a duplicate field label or API-name rename is rejected, the editor can switch to the conflicting field while retaining the original field URL. logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. A custom record type’s Record image setting cannot persist clearing a previously selected Files field to None, even after the automatic update request completes.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The reported successful mutation returns the previous identifier despite the form submitting null, locating the failure on the nullable object-metadata update/override boundary. Pinned source explicitly retains null overrides in computeMetadataOverridesBlob and resolves them in getEffectiveImageIdentifierFieldMetadataId; a deterministic source defect explaining this report is not established. Do not conflate this with the independently confirmed metadata-event null-override display bug. Unresolved source cause: the source boundary is identified, but available evidence does not establish the distinct underlying defect.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s approved-domain settings use a verification email to register a domain for workspace access. Approved-domain duplicate validation compares domain text case-sensitively, so changing capitalization allows separate saved registrations of the same domain.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Approved domains are submitted/stored as the entered string without a common lowercase canonicalization before uniqueness comparison. Case-sensitive comparison therefore permits domains differing only by case.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s approved-domain settings use a verification email to register a domain for workspace access. Approved-domain duplicate validation compares domain text case-sensitively, so changing capitalization allows separate saved registrations of the same domain.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty uses selection dropdowns both for workflow inputs and for assigning permission roles. An unconfigured or no-longer-eligible Select value is displayed as the first available option without saving that choice. Workflow Form sources, Form answers, action mappings (saved input values or references) and time zones can therefore look configured but submit no value; role selectors can display a different role from the saved assignment. A sole unsaved option can also be disabled, preventing explicit selection.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Select derives selectedOption by matching value, then falls back to options[0] when no emptyOption is supplied. This fallback neither changes the stored value nor calls onChange. Its single-option disabled condition additionally treats the visually selected fallback as a real selection. Workflow and role callers pass unset or filtered-out values into this shared behavior.
reproductionPaths: Twenty uses selection dropdowns both for workflow inputs and for assigning permission roles. Disabling member applicability for an already assigned custom role makes the member’s Permissions role selector display a different role, although the original assignment remains intact.

Twenty uses selection dropdowns both for workflow inputs and for assigning permission roles. Disabling API-key applicability on an already assigned custom role makes the API-key editor display a different role, while the saved role assignment remains unchanged.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. An AI tool can define its input parameters from the types in its function code. Disabling and re-enabling its trigger replaces that inferred input structure with an empty one even though the typed code has not changed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The AI tool-trigger toggle calls onChange with DEFAULT_TOOL_TRIGGER_SETTINGS when enabled and null when disabled. Re-enabling recreates the default empty inputSchema instead of restoring the previously configured parameters.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s AI tools infer configurable parameters from typed function code. Disable and re-enable an AI tool trigger without changing that code: the saved parameters disappear and its sample input becomes empty. Editing the source makes parameter inference run again; actual AI invocation was not tested.

logicalBugs.rootCause: The Relations Type column sorts field.type, which is RELATION or MORPH_RELATION, while its displayed label is derived from relation cardinality (Has many/Belongs to one). Sorting that metadata type cannot alphabetize the displayed relationship types.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model Relations table lists fields that link records. Click its Type heading in either direction: the arrow changes, but Has many and Belongs to one rows stay interleaved in the same order rather than sorting by those displayed types.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can show commands as pinned header buttons or inside a command menu. Pinning a standard command such as Export view can disappear from the saving browser header or fail to appear in another open browser. The stale unpinned state can survive ordinary reload even though the saved customization remains present.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The commandMenuItem branch of MetadataEventPublisher uses enrichCommandMenuItemEventWithResolvedNavigation instead of the generic overridable-record projection. That helper returns non-navigation commands without merging overrides. Base isPinned:false can therefore overwrite the saved effective pinned command in the frontend metadata store and its IndexedDB cache. Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can show commands as pinned header buttons or inside a command menu. Pinning a Companies header action in one browser saves correctly, but another signed-in browser keeps an outdated header even after refreshing.

A fresh Invite load has an empty role list until visiting Roles populates those atoms, so labels fall back to Default role and the selector disables.

A long record or settings-page title squeezes the page header action area until controls overlap. Record ellipsis can cover the position counter, and settings Edit actions can overlap the title instead of remaining separately usable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: PageCardHeader allocates its left breadcrumb/title track as minmax(0, auto) and its right action track as minmax(0, 1fr). The right wrapper can shrink to zero while its child controls retain intrinsic widths. A long left title therefore leaves action children painting over one another rather than reserving their required width.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s layout customization shows a record title beside an Edit actions button. At phone width, a long title extends underneath the button label and makes both texts hard to read. The button still opens its panel; a short title or desktop width avoids the overlap.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. Clearing a navigation link URL immediately restores its previous contents, so typing a replacement appends it to the old URL instead of replacing it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SidePanelEditLinkItemView binds its text input to urlEditInput || selectedItem.link. Clearing the draft to an empty string immediately falls back to the saved URL; subsequent typing appends to that restored value instead of replacing it.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s layout customization lets users organize workspace navigation into links and folders. Clearing a navigation link URL immediately restores its previous contents, so typing a replacement appends it to the old URL instead of replacing it.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Deleting a custom record type in one authenticated browser session crashes an already-open data-model diagram in another session instead of removing the deleted record type’s step.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Diagram relation/node rendering assumes referenced object and field metadata remain present. A remote deletion updates the metadata collection while existing graph nodes/edges can still hold deleted references, and unguarded relation access can throw before the asynchronous Dagre graph rebuild replaces them. The exact throw site during the captured race remains source-inferred. Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Deleting a custom record type in one authenticated browser session crashes an already-open data-model diagram in another session instead of removing the deleted record type’s step.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty settings have separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. Uploading an ordinary text file as a Profile picture or Workspace picture succeeds without rejection and saves an unusable placeholder, including replacing a verified valid image. Reload retains the broken picture; genuine images work and text disguised with an image extension is rejected.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Both workspace-logo and member-avatar upload mutations call FileCorePictureService.uploadCorePicture. That shared method calls general extractFileInfoOrThrow but never enforces an image MIME/type contract before writing a permanent CorePicture file. Valid plain text consequently passes identification and becomes the saved logo/avatar reference.
reproductionPaths: Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. Uploading an ordinary text file through Profile picture saves it as the avatar and replaces a previously valid image with a persistent placeholder, without rejection feedback.

Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. General settings accepts an ordinary text file as the workspace picture, persisting an unusable logo without rejection feedback and allowing replacement of a valid image.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s approved-domain settings use a verification email to register a domain for workspace access. A long domain on the New Approved Access Domain form squeezes the adjacent email-prefix input until its typed value is invisible.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The page passes the full domain as TextInput rightAdornment. The adornment has a fit-content minimum width and fixed height beside a shrinkable input with no protected readable minimum width.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s approved-domain settings use a verification email to register a domain for workspace access. A long domain on the New Approved Access Domain form squeezes the adjacent email-prefix input until its typed value is invisible.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. Rejecting a role save with an empty name leaves the Save button spinning until a later successful save.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsRole sets isSaving before validating the role name. The empty-name return happens before the try/finally that resets it.
reproductionPaths: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. Rejecting a role save with an empty name leaves the Save button spinning until a later successful save.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Choose None for Companies’ Record image setting and let it save. The saved choice is correct, but a background settings update can make the open page show the old domain-based logo again. This is a display reversal after a successful clear, not the custom-record-type case where clearing fails to save.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The pinned metadata-event publisher skips explicit null overrides with isDefined, leaving the standard Company object’s old base image-field ID in the pushed update. It races the correct null save response in the browser store.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Companies saves Record image None correctly, but its pushed metadata event can restore the old domain-logo display in the open settings page.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can show commands as pinned header buttons or inside a command menu. After a desktop record or workflow surface is resized to tablet or mobile layout, eligible actions disappear from both the pinned toolbar and the default command menu. Searching or reloading restores actions such as Test, Deactivate, See Runs and Company commands.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Mobile unmounts the pinned toolbar measurement producer, but shared inline-layout state retains desktop widths. The default menu incorrectly excludes actions it believes remain inline.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can show commands as pinned header buttons or inside a command menu. After desktop-to-tablet resizing, eligible pinned Company actions disappear from both toolbar and default command menu until search or reload.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. Reloading a role tab keeps its Assignment or Settings fragment in the URL but displays Permissions instead.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The role initialization effect writes Permissions after role loading, competing with URL-driven tab selection. The exact effect scheduling is inferred; the settled tab/address mismatch is observed.
reproductionPaths: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. Reloading a role tab keeps its Assignment or Settings fragment in the URL but displays Permissions instead.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Profile settings edit the signed-in member’s name and picture. The autosaving Profile name editor silently leaves a cleared required Last Name in the field without indicating that it will not save; reload restores the saved name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NameFields suppresses autosave when either required name is empty, while its inputs render no validation state and its save path exposes no explicit saving or success feedback.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Profile settings edit the signed-in member’s name and picture. The autosaving Profile name editor silently leaves a cleared required Last Name in the field without indicating that it will not save; reload restores the saved name.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. With no existing profile picture, an oversized genuine PNG can leave an upload pending while its offered Abort action is disabled.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ImageInput disables Abort whenever pictureURI is empty, including an active upload before any first picture exists. The request cancellation handler exists but cannot be reached through the disabled control.
reproductionPaths: Twenty settings provide separate picture upload controls for the signed-in member and the workspace. With no existing profile picture, an oversized genuine PNG can leave an upload pending while its offered Abort action is disabled.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. Rapid repeated submission of one valid API-key creation form creates multiple distinct persisted keys.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The creation form has no in-flight guard or pending disabled/loading state. Save and Enter can reenter the asynchronous creation handler, and each invocation inserts a separate key.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. Rapid repeated submission of one valid API-key creation form creates multiple distinct persisted keys.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Skills Name sorting orders hidden API names rather than the displayed Skill labels.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Name column displays label but configures the client sorter to use name, the hidden API identifier, overriding the server label ordering.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Skills Name sorting orders hidden API names rather than the displayed Skill labels.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. After same-session role assignment, entering the object-rule wizard overwrites pending global permission restrictions, so saving retains the old globals instead of the intended restrictions.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Immediate assignment stores a different member representation in role state. Network-only GetRoles on wizard mounts sees a deep difference and overwrites the entire dirty draft, discarding pending global restrictions. The resets are observed; precise callback ordering is inferred.
reproductionPaths: Twenty roles determine which settings, actions and data workspace members can access. After same-session role assignment, entering the object-rule wizard overwrites pending global permission restrictions, so saving retains the old globals instead of the intended restrictions.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Editing and reopening a custom Percentage field exposes floating-point precision noise in the input, such as 0.12345 becoming 0.12345000000000002. The effect persists after reload even though normal field display rounds the value.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The editor multiplies a stored fractional percentage by 100 and stringifies it without precision cleanup; normal display uses a formatter.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Entering 0.12345 and reopening displays 0.12345000000000002, with or without reload.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. A populated field that can link to several record types lacks the pencil button normally shown on hover in a full record page or side panel. Clicking the surrounding field still opens its picker. This concerns the missing edit affordance, not a completely unusable relationship editor.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The detail icon selector handles RELATION but omits MORPH_RELATION. Details render an edit button only when an icon exists; tables provide a pencil fallback. The outer detail container still opens the picker.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Hover a populated field that can link to several record types on a full record page or side panel. Its edit-pencil icon is missing, although clicking the surrounding field still opens the picker.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. At phone width, the Name column of the record type’s Relations table collapses. Relationship labels draw beneath neighboring application badges rather than remaining readable in their own column.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Relations grid consumes fixed width for other columns before allocating the Name column, leaving zero width at the tested viewport. Visible overflow draws labels under App badges.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model Relations table lists fields that link records. At phone width its Name column collapses, and relationship labels draw beneath application badges rather than remaining separately readable. Row clicks still open the correct field editor.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Multi-value field previews in Data model settings ignore the configured maximum number of items, showing more sample entries than actual record entry allows.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The preview receives the field metadata but its example values remain static; rendering displays every supplied sample item rather than limiting the sample to the configured maximum.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Set the maximum number of items allowed in a multi-value field, such as an Emails field limited to one address. The settings preview still displays more sample items than the configured limit, although actual record entry enforces it.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Reopening an ordinary saved relationship shows the destination’s internal API name, capitalized, instead of its configured display label. The wrong label appears in both the relationship editor and its preview.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Ordinary RELATION branch looks up destination field but selects relation.targetFieldMetadata.name, then capitalize; both destination input and preview consume that default. Neighboring morph branch correctly reads targetFieldMetadata.label.
reproductionPaths: Twenty relationship fields can define a reverse field on the destination record type. Reopen an ordinary saved relationship: its destination-field editor and preview show the capitalized internal API name instead of the saved display label. The stored labels and links remain correct.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Edit one record-type setting, such as its name, then start typing a newer Plural or Description value while the first save finishes. Completion of that earlier save resets the form and overwrites the newer typing; a later save can persist the damaged text.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Blur starts save with captured whole formValues; after mutation and awaited metadata query, formConfig.reset(formValues) restores older snapshot over live edits. Following blur stores altered value.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Completion of an earlier object-settings save resets the whole form, overwriting newer Plural or Description typing.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Correcting a transient typo in Bulk edit changes an existing Select or Multi-select option’s internal identity and erases records’ saved selections despite unchanged final labels.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Bulk textarea reparses each intermediate change against the latest draft options, losing original option identities. Restoring the original label generates another UUID. Server enum migration maps old values only by matching UUID and drops unmapped old storage values.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Correcting a transient typo in Bulk edit changes an existing Select or Multi-select option’s internal identity and erases records’ saved selections despite unchanged final labels.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Clearing Skill Instructions saves empty rich-text markup as required content, leaving the Skill active with a blank editor.
logicalBugs.rootCause:
The rich-text editor emits HTML, so an empty document becomes the nonempty string

. Client trim().length checks and server isNonEmptyString validation accept the markup without checking semantic editor emptiness.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Clearing Skill Instructions saves empty rich-text markup as required content, leaving the Skill active with a blank editor.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. The Objects list permanently removes a deactivated custom record type directly, while its Settings page requires typed confirmation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The inactive row-menu callback calls the object deletion hook directly. The object-detail Settings flow opens a confirmation dialog before calling the same deletion hook, so the destructive list entry point skips that safeguard.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. The Objects list permanently removes a deactivated custom record type directly, while its Settings page requires typed confirmation.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. The data-model diagram renders an invisible SVG over the mobile Back to Objects link, so pointer clicks leave the diagram open.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The relation-marker SVG is absolutely positioned at top:0/left:0 without explicit dimensions or disabled pointer events. Its diagram container is not positioned. The observed SVG occupies the viewport’s top-left 300×150 area and receives pointer events over the breadcrumb instead of its working link.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. The data-model diagram renders an invisible SVG over the mobile Back to Objects link, so pointer clicks leave the diagram open.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Opening an inactive custom record type’s settings shows an enabled Deactivate action that leaves it inactive and returns to the object list.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ObjectSettings renders the Danger zone without consulting objectMetadataItem.isActive, and its Deactivate handler always sends isActive:false before navigating to the list. The inactive-inclusive detail lookup and duplicate-name Open path allow the same component to render for an inactive object.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Opening an inactive custom record type’s settings shows an enabled Deactivate action that leaves it inactive and returns to the object list.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. A relationship can allow links to several destination record types, with a corresponding reverse field on each destination. Deleting one reverse field can hide the surviving relationship on its source settings page and leave another reverse field incomplete until refresh, even though another destination remains.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The metadata query collapses per-destination rows to one representative, which inverse relation lookups also reference. Deletion removes only the chosen inverse and paired source leg, while client per-row cleanup does not promote or reload the surviving collapsed leg. A missing representative makes the remaining relation lookup incomplete until metadata reload.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can link one source record type to several destination types, with a reverse field on each destination. Delete one destination’s reverse field: settings can hide the surviving source relationship and remove the remaining reverse field’s destination/type labels. Refresh restores their management display; this is not deletion of the whole relationship.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s approved-domain settings use a verification email to register a domain for workspace access. The approved-domain form says the value must be smaller than 256 characters, but a 256-character domain produces no domain-length error. The separate required email control still prevents saving the tested blank-email form.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The approved-domain form states smaller than 256 but applies inclusive max256. A separate required email guard blocks the original empty-email submission.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s approved-domain settings use a verification email to register a domain for workspace access. Enter an approved domain at the stated length boundary. The form says the value must be shorter than 256 characters but accepts a 256-character domain without a length error; the separate required-email rule still blocks the tested blank-email submission.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. At narrow widths, the GraphQL and REST playground breadcrumb (page navigation link) omits its MCP & APIs destination text and shows only Back to. The incomplete back link still navigates correctly.
logicalBugs.rootCause: MobileBreadcrumb derives its back-link text only when previousLink.children is a nonempty string. The playground pages pass <Trans> React elements for breadcrumb children, so text becomes empty and the mobile back control omits its destination label.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. Open the GraphQL or REST API playground at phone width. Its breadcrumb (page navigation link) reads only Back to without the MCP & APIs destination name, although the link still navigates back.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Add trailing spaces when entering or changing a custom record type’s singular label. Its automatically generated plural becomes malformed; saving trims the singular but keeps the malformed plural in settings and the page heading after reload.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The singular label change handler pluralizes raw untrimmed text, so trailing spaces become part of the automatically derived plural. Server sanitization trims final strings but cannot reconstruct the intended plural after pluralization has already transformed the whitespace-bearing value.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Adding trailing spaces to a custom record type’s singular label generates a plural such as County s. Saving trims the singular but retains the malformed plural in Settings and the heading after reload. Padded object creation also reproduces the malformed plural.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Clear every destination in a relationship-field editor. Its destination selector is empty, but the preview still names an unrelated record type instead of showing an unconfigured relationship.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsDataModelFieldRelationFormCard falls back to an available object when it cannot resolve the selected destination. An intentionally empty destination selection therefore previews that fallback object rather than an empty/unconfigured relation.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Clearing every record link destination leaves a preview card naming an unrelated object even though the destination selector is empty.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. The reported New API key form presents an apparently actionable Save with an empty Name, but clicking does not explain the missing required value.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The API-key creation handler returns immediately for an empty name, but the Save button does not reflect a required-name validation state and no error is rendered on that return. The apparently actionable submission produces no explanation.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s API keys give external software access to workspace data. Leave the Name empty on the reported New API key form and click its apparently actionable Save control. The form does not explain the missing required value; this concerns that reported actionable-control state.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Editing a fresh custom Number field can show a missing-target metadata error while displaying the value locally, then reopen empty after reload.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Record update performs optimistic relation synchronization before persistence; that code requires complete field metadata and throws if it cannot resolve a referenced field. A newly created Number field can be present in one metadata projection but absent in the relation synchronizer, aborting the update after an optimistic value was displayed. Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Create a custom Number field and edit its value on a record. A missing-field-metadata error can appear after the value is shown locally, and reloading reveals it was not saved.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. A custom record type’s New action repeatedly fails with an error and no creation panel after a field-metadata error; the prerequisite state and later recovery remain unresolved.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The New action builds record defaults and query projections from the current object/field metadata. In the supplied unresolved field-metadata state those required lookups fail before opening the creation panel. No exact corrupt field or deterministic root-producing transition is established; fresh equivalent objects work and the original recovered spontaneously. Unresolved source cause: the source boundary is identified, but available evidence does not establish the distinct underlying defect.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Use New on the reported custom record type after a field-metadata error. An error appears and no creation panel opens. The prerequisite damaged state was not determined, equivalent fresh types work, and the original later recovered.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Editing Workspace Instructions and immediately opening Skills loses the edit without a save prompt or warning. Returning to Overview restores the previous instructions.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Workspace Instructions uses a debounced update in SettingsAiOverviewTab without flushing it on tab unmount. Immediate AI-tab navigation disposes the pending callback before it saves the entered content.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s AI settings contain reusable Skills and workspace-wide instructions for AI features. Editing Workspace Instructions and immediately opening Skills loses the edit without a save prompt or warning. Returning to Overview restores the previous instructions.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. When a Select field has a default option, saving any change to its options in Settings > Data model (even renaming an unrelated option) sets every record whose value was empty (null) to the default option. Data the user never touched is silently changed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Select option migration recreates the enum column with its configured default and copies only non-null old values. Existing NULL records are not copied and therefore acquire that default when any option edit rebuilds the column.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. When a Select field has a default option, saving any change to its options in Settings > Data model (even renaming an unrelated option) sets every record whose value was empty (null) to the default option. Data the user never touched is silently changed.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After UI deactivation and reactivation, a custom record type’s Search section stays enabled but omits the indexed-field names, static weights and data types until full reload.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Object reactivation writes the mutation response directly as FlatObjectMetadataItem into the metadata store, while the full hydration mapper normalizes search/index field metadata. Search information resolves through canonical metadata, so the differently shaped immediate response can temporarily omit its indexed fields until a full reload. Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. After UI deactivation and reactivation, a custom record type’s Search section stays enabled but omits the indexed-field names, static weights and data types until full reload.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Profile settings edit the signed-in member’s name and picture. Profile names autosave only after a delay. Navigating to another settings page immediately after editing cancels the pending change without saving or warning.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NameFields schedules valid autosave through a 500ms debounce and returns debouncedUpdate.cancel from effect cleanup. Navigating away before the callback fires cancels the mutation instead of flushing the latest name.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Profile settings edit the signed-in member’s name and picture. Profile names autosave only after a delay. Navigating to another settings page immediately after editing cancels the pending change without saving or warning.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. The permanent-erasure retention-days input in Settings Security has no accessible name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SettingsOptionCardContentCounter renders its title as ordinary text separate from SettingsCounter. It passes value/change bounds but no aria-label, labelledby or connected label ID to the underlying retention input, leaving the erasure field without an accessible name.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. Open the permanent-erasure retention-days setting in Security. Its numeric input has no accessible name connecting it to the setting’s visible title.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. In the default light theme, Settings descriptions and sidebar section labels have insufficient text contrast.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Settings card descriptions use font.color.light and sidebar section titles use font.color.tertiary on the light backgrounds without sufficient contrast for their small normal-weight text. These shared theme tokens produce the observed #999/#b3b3b3 foreground colors.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. In the default light theme, Settings descriptions and sidebar section labels have insufficient text contrast.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. A valid pending Workspace name edit is lost when the user immediately switches from General to Security settings.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NameField debounces workspace-name persistence for 500ms and returns debouncedUpdate.cancel from its effect cleanup. Switching away immediately cancels the pending save, discarding the local name edit.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Data model settings define record types, such as Companies, and the fields stored on their records. A valid pending Workspace name edit is lost when the user immediately switches from General to Security settings.
